Hi, I'm the greatest person to walk this earth. But that's irrelevant to this.

The majority of subverses on voat are quite lackluster in CSS, so I've decided to make a tutorial series showing off simple things hoping that people can learn from them and apply them to more complicated stuff.

Section 1: Aim of this tutorial

The aim of this tutorial for today is to modify the score bar. We will do all of the following:

  • Reposition the scorebar
  • Change the size of the scorebar
  • Change the colour of the scorebar
  • Changing how curvy the edges of the scorebar are

Section 2: Default properties

The default properties of the scorebar CSS are in the following sections. Copying them into your stylesheet as-is won't do anything right now, but you can make it happen by changing the various properties or adding new ones, as we will discuss in this tutorial. It is not necessary to copy the following code it's just helpful if you're a newbie.

2.a: Scorebar

.scorebar{
 border-radius:2px;
 float:left;
 height:51px;
 margin-right:12px;
 overflow:hidden;
 width:2px;
 cursor:help;
}

2.b: Upvotes

.scorebar-likes{
 background:#36627D;
 clear:both;
 width:100%;
}

2.c Downvotes

.scorebar-dislikes{
 background:#5A5196;
 border-top:1px solid #333;
 clear:both;
 width:100%;
}

Section 3: Method

By default, the scorebar is located to the right side of the voting buttons and score, and is separated into two coloured parts, blue for the percentage of upvotes and purple for the percentage of downvotes. The edges are slightly rounded, and it is 51 pixels tall and 2 pixels wide.

3.a: Repositioning the scorebar

Alright, first thing's first, let's change where the scorebar is located. At the moment, it's located to the right side of the votes/score area. Let's try moving it to multiple places, to the far right of the entry, and to the left of the scrollbar. There are a few ways to go about doing this, the most obvious probably being the float: property.

If you haven't create a block with the .scorebar selector. If you don't understand what this means, that's okay, I will add comments to the first example explaining. (Comments are pieces of code that the computer ignores. In CSS a comment starts with /* and ends with */.

.scorebar{ /* The ".scorebar" is the selector. It tells the computer what it is looking for/. */
 /* The entire section of curly braces, also including the selector, is called a block. Properties (rules for CSS) go inside the curly brackets. */
}

At the moment, it's empty and won't do anything. Go to your .scorebar block and add float:right; between the curly braces:

.scorebar{
 float:right;
}

Tadaa! After you've saved your changes in the subverse settings, the scorebar will no longer be next to the voting area. It will now be, instead, located to the right side of the submission.

float: isn't the best way of doing this though -- for example, float:left; doesn't do anything, because it's already as far left as it's allowed to go -- other elements have already been floated left to take its place.

There are other ways to do it though. Delete the float:right; line from your .scorebar block, and create a new block with the selector .submission. Then, add a new property to .submission, position:relative;.

.submission{
 position:relative;
}

You won't notice anything change, but trust me, it is important to have that there. Next, go back to .scorebar and add the following properties position:absolute; which will let us put the element wherever we want, top:12px, left:12px. 

.scorebar{
 position:absolute;
 top:12px;
 left:18px;
}

This will position it with an absolute value of 12 pixels from the top and 16 pixels from the left, relative to the elements selected by .submission.

3.b: Resizing the element

Resizing is literally one of the easiest things you could possibly do with CSS. All you have to do is take the element you want and add two properties to it, height: and width:. There are other ways to do it for different situations, but this is the easiest and simplest way.

After the height: and width: properties, all you need to do is add the appropriate value (in this case a number) and the unit of measurement. Common units are px (pixels), % (percent), pt (points), and em (funky unit of measurement based off the letter m).

.scorebar{
 /* All your other code here */
 height:50px;
 width:50px;
}

There will be breakages with this. The element will take up too much space and cover other elements. There are a few different ways to fix this, a simple one is to simply add a big margin to the voting area. 

.midcol{
 margin-left:55px;
}

3.c: Changing the colour of the scrollbar

Once again, another easy task. Create two blocks with the selector .scorebar-likes for one and .scorebar-dislikes for the other.

.scorebar-likes{

}
.scorebar-dislikes{

}

Let's make upvotes in a bright blue and downvotes in a middle grey. Create a background: property and then add a colour of your choosing. Colours are specified a few ways using CSS, but the main way is using hex codes. w3schools provides a hex colour picker which will tell you the hex code for different colours. Simply paste these after the property (and don't forget to close with a semicolon). 

.scorebar-likes{
 background:#33AAFF;
}
.scorebar-dislikes{
 background:#888888;
}

And there you have it!

3.d: Changing the curviness of the edges

Thanks to a useful and fairly recent addition to CSS, it's possible to make the edges of an element rounded. I'm sure you've already seen this on your score 'bar' as you've been following this tutorial. The way to change the edginess, so to speak, is using the border-radius: property. There are several other properties almost identical to border-radius:, that are used to control specific corners, such as border-top-left-radius:, which controls the top-left corner.

Go to your .scorebar block again and add a border-radius: property. Use 0px (or just 0, as 0 is special in that it doesn't need a unit of measurement) or 50% for a circle. 

.scorebar{
 /* All your other code */
 border-radius:50%;
}

The shape will now be changed. Hooray!

Section 4: Final code

The final result for this is: 

.scorebar-likes{
 background:#33AAFF;
}
.scorebar-dislikes{
 background:#888888;
}
.submission{
 position:relative;
}
.midcol{
 margin-left:55px;
}
.scorebar{
 position:absolute;
 top:12px;
 left:18px;
 height:50px;
 width:50px;
 border-radius:50%;
}

You can see it over at /v/TSG3, where I will be applying all of my CSS changes done in these tutorials. Hope you've learnt something from my tutorials! Please leave any feedback/problems in the comments, I don't bite!

Efforts to stop impaired driving hampered by loopholes

Summery: Police are having problems apprehending impaired drivers in the first place. They can pull over cars they suspect of being impaired, but not those they don't suspect. About half of impaired drivers at road stop checks go undetected. Police believe random breath testing at any time will help catch impaired drivers, but the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms will block such warrantless stops. Doctor-patient confidentiality laws are also preventing physicians from informing police of suspected drunken drivers brought to the hospital after an accident.

tl;dr: Police want warrantless stops of unsuspected drivers and to see medical records for signs of impairment.
